title: Implement tier-aware LRU eviction for KV cache (respect pinned sessions + prefix cache)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Goal
Define and implement eviction selection logic for KV cache pages/blocks when the allocator is under pressure and compaction alone cannot reclaim contiguous space fast enough. Eviction must be tier-aware and LRU-based, must respect pinned sessions, and must be observable and safe (no correctness regressions).

Context
KV cache compaction reduces fragmentation but does not eliminate peak memory pressure during bursty decode + churn. Today we have opportunistic evictions in a few places (mostly “best effort”) that are hard to reason about and can happen at the worst time (mid-decode), creating tail spikes. This ticket formalizes a single eviction policy entry point and selection algorithm aligned with product tiers.

Policy requirements
1) Tier-aware
- Hosted (shared) tiers: eviction allowed for lower-priority traffic first to protect paid tiers and latency commitments.
- Dedicated: eviction should be conservative; prefer backpressure + compaction before evicting active decode. If eviction is needed, focus on preemptible/prefix-cache artifacts first.
- Private: default eviction disabled (or only prefix-cache eviction) unless explicitly configured.

2) LRU by sequence/session
- Primary ordering: least-recently-used “sequence group” (a session may have multiple sequences; treat as a unit for eviction fairness).
- Recency definition: last scheduler touch timestamp (decode step, prefill, or token emission) rather than wall-clock request arrival.
- Avoid pathological cases: long-running streaming sessions should not be evicted if pinned or high-tier; otherwise they may be evicted if they become cold.

3) Correctness + safety constraints
- Never evict pinned sessions (see pinned semantics below).
- Never evict while a relocation/compaction move is in-flight for that sequence (avoid races with page ownership changes).
- Eviction must be atomic from the scheduler’s perspective: after eviction, the sequence must be either (a) terminated with a clear error path, or (b) forced to recompute from a safe checkpoint (not in scope for initial release). For initial release we will terminate with a retryable error for evicted active sequences; prefix-cache artifacts can be dropped without surfacing an error.
- Explicitly define what can be evicted:
  a) Prefix cache pages (safe to drop; may increase compute)
  b) Inactive/idle sequences (waiting, queued, or disconnected)
  c) Active decode sequences (last resort; gated by tier + kill-switch)

Pinned sessions semantics
- “Pinned” means eviction-protected. Sources of pinning:
  - Internal: system/reserved workloads (control-plane health checks, eval canaries), enterprise SLO cohorts.
  - Customer: Dedicated/Private may have pinned workloads (e.g., long-lived agents) via config.
- Pinning should be implemented as a scheduler-visible attribute on the sequence group (pin_reason, pinned_until optional).
- Pinned does not mean “infinite”: if we hit hard OOM territory we must prefer backpressure/request shedding at admission rather than violating pinning. This ticket ensures eviction never breaks pinning; overload handling remains in scheduler/admission.

Interfaces / integration points
- New eviction entry point: KvArena::evict(target_bytes, policy_ctx) -> EvictResult
- policy_ctx inputs:
  - tier (hosted_free/hosted_pro/dedicated/private)
  - model/profile (for per-model defaults)
  - allow_active_decode_eviction (bool; default false except hosted_free)
  - eviction_watermark (soft/hard)
  - now_ts (monotonic)
- Scheduler hook: scheduler requests eviction only at safe boundaries (prefill->decode transition, decode step boundary) per ENG-4824. Allocator may request eviction only when it cannot satisfy allocation and compaction budget is exhausted.

Selection algorithm (proposed)
- Build candidate sets in descending preference:
  1) Prefix cache artifacts (unshared, then shared; avoid thrashing by applying a minimum age)
  2) Non-pinned idle sequences in lowest tier first (hosted_free -> hosted_pro -> dedicated)
  3) Non-pinned active decode sequences only if allow_active_decode_eviction is true and we’re past hard watermark
- Within each set, order by LRU (oldest last_touch first), break ties by largest bytes to free (greedy) to minimize number of evictions.
- Enforce per-eviction cap: max_sequences_per_tick and max_bytes_per_tick to avoid long stalls.

Observability (must-have)
- Counters:
  - kv_evictions_total{tier,reason,target_type}
  - kv_evicted_bytes_total{tier,reason,target_type}
  - kv_eviction_denied_total{reason} (e.g., pinned_only_remaining, in_flight_move, policy_disabled)
- Histograms:
  - kv_eviction_duration_ms
- Tracing span per eviction batch with exemplar linking to tail latency traces.

Config / kill switches
- Feature flag: kv.eviction.enabled (default off in Private; on in Hosted with conservative defaults)
- Flags:
  - kv.eviction.allow_active_decode
  - kv.eviction.hard_watermark_ratio
  - kv.eviction.soft_watermark_ratio
  - kv.eviction.max_bytes_per_tick
  - kv.eviction.max_sequences_per_tick
- All config must be safe to flip at runtime via ENG-4826 plumbing.

Testing plan (correctness-focused)
Unit tests
- Candidate selection respects tier ordering.
- LRU ordering correctness with synthetic timestamps.
- Pinned sessions are never selected.
- In-flight move sequences are never selected.
- Prefix cache eviction does not terminate active sequences.

Integration / stress tests (Anika + Marcus)
- Mixed churn + cancellations while eviction occurs (regression for the relocation/cancel race).
- Long-lived streaming session pinned + background churn: ensure no eviction and no deadlock.
- Active decode eviction path (when enabled) returns retryable error and cleans up pages; no leaks.
- Metrics assertions: eviction counters increment; denied counters for pinned-only scenario.

Acceptance criteria
- Under synthetic hard-pressure scenario, allocator can reclaim target_bytes via eviction without OOM.
- No pinned session eviction in any test.
- No crashes / memory leaks in stress suite (10k sequences churn, 30+ minutes run).
- Clear metrics and traces for each eviction batch.
- Defaults reviewed by SRE + Product for Hosted/Dedicated behaviors.

Links
- ADR (eviction policy): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-kv-eviction-policy.json
- Design doc: sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kv-cache-compaction-design.json
- Related tickets: ENG-4822 (metrics), ENG-4823 (compaction worker), ENG-4824 (scheduler hook), ENG-4826 (kill switch/config)

Notes / open questions
- Should we treat “prefix cache” as a separate tier dimension (e.g., always evict prefix cache before any session KV)? Proposed: yes.
- For active decode eviction: do we want to attempt resumable retry (recompute) later? Out of scope for runtime-1.22; file follow-up if needed.
- Dedicated defaults: Product leaning toward allow_active_decode=false always; confirm with Lauren + SRE once benchmark canary results are in.
comments: 2026-01-10 (Talia Benson): Created as part of ENG-4821 epic. Please keep policy decisions aligned with ADR; SRE wants explicit metrics names for dashboards.

2026-01-14 (Omar El-Sayed): Drafted selection sets: prefix-cache first, then idle sequences, then active decode behind gate. Need scheduler to provide safe boundary hooks (ENG-4824) to avoid mid-step evictions.

2026-01-18 (Sean Gallagher): From SRE side: active-decode eviction must be rare and loud. Please add kv_eviction_denied_total so we can tell the difference between “policy prevented” and “no pressure.” Also ensure trace exemplars exist so we can correlate to p99 spikes.

2026-01-22 (Lauren Bishop): Dedicated: default should not evict active decode. If we must evict, prefer dropping prefix cache and idle sequences only. We can tolerate some recompute; we cannot tolerate user-visible errors for steady workloads.

2026-01-27 (Samir Qureshi): Added guardrail: skip sequences with in-flight relocation. Without that we can race page ownership changes. We’ll track relocation state in sequence metadata and gate candidates.

2026-02-02 (Anika Gupta): Test plan suggestion: add adversarial cancellation during eviction selection to ensure cleanup doesn’t double-free. Also add pinned + idle mix to confirm only non-pinned are chosen.

2026-02-06 (Omar El-Sayed): Implementation mostly complete locally. One nuance: session grouping for LRU. We’ll evict by sequence_group_id (shared across tool calls / streaming reconnect). Need to confirm how scheduler updates last_touch (decode step boundary).

2026-02-10 (Noah Patel): Review note: define explicit error semantics for active eviction (retryable, not internal error). Also require invariant: eviction cannot occur while a sequence is in 'decoding' critical section unless scheduler boundary says it’s safe. Please ensure we have asserts in debug builds.
